simple.meaning: מֶרְקָחָה (merqâchâh) is a Hebrew action word meaning “abstractly, a seasoning (with spicery); concretely, an unguentkettle (for preparing spiced oil).” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 2 times in Job, Ezekiel, beginning at Job 41:23. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מֶרְקָחָה (H4841) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: מֶרְקָחָה (merqâchâh) / H4841 is traced through Job 41:23, Ezekiel 24:10 with source-language evidence and verse context.
